haiku-low.q1: They sign in as the linked user. Lookup is by Google's permanent sub, not email, so the changed Gmail address does not matter.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the existing account's password on the confirm page. After the right password, the identity row is inserted and the pending record deleted, then start_session runs.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds to failed_logins and reshows the form; the pending link stays until its 10-minute TTL. On the fifth, the account locks for 15 minutes, the pending record is deleted, and the link is discarded.
haiku-low.q4: Verified email with no matching user: one transaction creates a passwordless, email-verified user and links the Google account, then signs in. Unverified email: redirect to /login, pointing to email and password; nothing is created.
haiku-low.q5: Both cases show the state error page, nothing changes. A late callback finds its Redis record expired after 600 s; a repeated load finds it already consumed by GETDEL.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row with a new sid cookie, via start_session. The old sid session row is deleted, so the browser's previous sid is replaced.
haiku-low.q7: Neither is required. It needs a valid sid session for the user who started, and no email match. If the Google account is linked to someone else, Settings refuses with an already-linked-to-someone-else message.
haiku-low.q8: State, nonce and code_verifier are in the Redis record goog:auth:sha256(state), with bind. GETDEL removes it at the first callback, otherwise TTL 600 s expires it. Cookie g_bind is cleared at callback.
haiku-low.q9: Redis record goog:pending:sha256(pending id) holds sub, target user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the g_pending cookie's random id. DEL on success, lockout, cancel or race refusal; otherwise TTL 600 s.
haiku-low.q10: In the google_identities PostgreSQL table. sub is its primary key (one Google account, one user); user_id is UNIQUE (one user, one Google account), with cascade delete.
haiku-low.q11: The user is redirected to the origin page (/login or Settings) with: we could not complete Google sign-in, try again or use email and password. The code is not retried; the cause is logged.
haiku-low.q12: The Redis record's mode field (login or link) is set at start from the entry point. Link mode requires the current sid session to be valid and its user to equal record.user_id, the user who started.

sonnet.q1: Nothing changes for them. Accounts are identified by `sub`, not email, and no email is stored. The `sub` is found in google_identities, so they sign in as the linked user via start_session.
sonnet.q2: They must confirm with the existing account's password. The callback saves a pending record (sub, user_id, next; TTL 600 s) and sets the g_pending cookie. It redirects to /auth/google/confirm. On the right password the identity row is inserted, pending is deleted, and start_session runs. A matching verified email alone is not enough.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins, the form is re-shown, and the pending record stays (TTL keeps running, not extended). On the fifth wrong password, locked_until is set to now + 15 min and failed_logins is reset to 0. The pending record is deleted, g_pending is cleared, and the 'Account temporarily locked' page is shown. The half-finished link is discarded, and the user must wait 15 minutes and start again.
sonnet.q4: If the email is verified and matches no user, one transaction creates the user (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at = now, other columns default) and inserts the google_identities row. Then start_session runs. If Google says the email is not verified, the user is redirected to /login with a message to use email and password. Nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: The Redis record has a 600 s TTL, so after 12 minutes it is expired. A second load of the same URL finds the record already consumed by GETDEL. Either way the record is not found, so the error page appears ('this sign-in link is invalid or expired'). Nothing changes, and the g_bind cookie is cleared.
sonnet.q6: It calls the same start_session(user_id) as POST /login. It deletes the old sid session row, inserts a new sessions row, sets the sid cookie, and redirects to next if it is a relative path, otherwise to /home. The browser then holds only sid, because g_bind and g_pending are cleared. Link mode does not call start_session.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email match are needed. The signed-in session already proves who the user is, and emails need not match. If the sub is already linked to another user, it is refused. The user goes back to Settings with the message 'this Google account is already linked to someone else', and nothing changes.
sonnet.q8: They are kept in a Redis record at goog:auth:<sha256(state)>. It also holds mode, user_id, next, origin and bind. The record has a 600 s TTL. It is removed by GETDEL at the first callback, valid or not, or else by TTL expiry.
sonnet.q9: It is held in a Redis record at goog:pending:<sha256(pending id)>, holding sub, target user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the random pending id in the g_pending cookie. It is deleted (DEL) on success, lockout, cancel or race refusal. Otherwise it expires after the 600 s TTL, which is never extended.
sonnet.q10: It is stored in the PostgreSQL table google_identities (sub, user_id, linked_at). sub is the PRIMARY KEY, so one Google account links to at most one user. user_id is NOT NULL UNIQUE, so one user has at most one Google account. A unique violation is treated as the matching refusal.
sonnet.q11: The user is redirected to the origin page (/login or Settings) with the message 'we could not complete Google sign-in, try again or use email and password'. Nothing changes and the cause is logged. The code is not retried.
sonnet.q12: The record.mode in the Redis auth record (login or link) tells it apart. For a link, the record stores user_id = the session user at start. The callback requires the current sid session to be valid and its user to equal record.user_id. Otherwise it redirects to /login with a retry message.
